models_evaluated: deep learning patient-specific dose prediction model for automatic radiotherapy planning

links.outcome: Overall plan quality (PQM) of DL-assisted automatic plans versus manual clinical plans on the same patients
links.effect: PQM 40.7 ± 13.1 manual vs 40.8 ± 13.5 automatic, equivalent quality; planning time 103.1 to 32.6 min (P<0.001); MUs 789.9 to 692.5 (P<0.001).
links.quote: The average PQM score was 40.7 ± 13.1 for manual plans and 40.8 ± 13.5 for automatic plans, and they had equivalent overall plan quality.

links.outcome: Expert clinician review of AI-generated plans for clinical acceptability
links.effect: Automatic plans clinically acceptable in 88% of reviews (176/200) by four expert reviewers; all accepted after fine tuning.
links.quote: In qualitative evaluation, automatic plans were deemed to be clinically acceptable for treatment in 88% of reviews (176/200), and all were accepted after fine tuning.

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates a deep learning tool for automatic radiotherapy treatment planning in lung cancer, assessing plan quality, efficiency, and clinical acceptability via expert review against manual plans.
